name: Mykonos
tagline: The Cyclades' most famous party island, its whitewashed lanes and windmills beautiful beyond the beach clubs and nightlife that made it internationally famous.
highlight: Little Venice's waterfront houses, their balconies hanging directly over the sea, lit warm at sunset alongside the row of historic windmills above.
shortDescription: Greece's most famous nightlife island, its beautiful whitewashed old town and windmills often overshadowed by its reputation for beach clubs and parties.
metaDescription: A Mykonos travel guide: Mykonos Town, the windmills, Delos, the best beaches, when to go and a practical three-day itinerary.
knownFor: Beach clubs, the windmills, Little Venice

image.alt: The windmills of Kato Mili above Mykonos Town

intro: Mykonos built its international reputation on beach clubs and nightlife starting in the 1960s, when the island became a genuine magnet for a jet-set crowd seeking sun and freedom that mainland Greece's more conservative culture didn't offer at the time. That reputation persists today, and the island remains one of the Mediterranean's most famous party destinations.

What that reputation tends to obscure is Mykonos Town itself, a gorgeous labyrinth of whitewashed cube houses, narrow marble-paved lanes designed centuries ago to confuse pirates, and the iconic row of windmills overlooking Little Venice's waterfront homes.

The island rewards visitors willing to look past the beach-club scene toward its genuine architectural beauty, its quieter northern beaches and Ano Mera's more traditional inland village, alongside the easy day trip to Delos, one of the ancient world's most sacred and significant islands.

whyVisit.intro: Mykonos' case is that no other Greek island pairs this famous a nightlife scene with this much genuine architectural beauty and ancient history alongside it.

points.title: Mykonos Town is one of the Cyclades' most beautiful old towns
points.text: Its labyrinthine whitewashed lanes and Little Venice waterfront rival any island's old town, beach clubs aside.

points.title: The nightlife is world famous
points.text: From sunset beach bars to late-night clubs, Mykonos' reputation as a party island is well earned for those seeking it.

points.title: Delos adds genuine ancient significance
points.text: A short boat trip reaches one of the ancient Greek world's most sacred islands, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

points.title: The beaches are excellent
points.text: From organised beach clubs to quieter northern coves, Mykonos' coastline offers real range beyond the famous party beaches.

points.title: It pairs well with Santorini
points.text: A short ferry or flight connects the two most famous Cyclades islands into an easy combined itinerary.

attractionsIntro: Mykonos' essential sights, from its famous windmills to the ancient island of Delos just offshore.

attractions.name: Mykonos Town (Chora)
attractions.text: A gorgeous maze of whitewashed cube houses and narrow marble lanes, deliberately laid out centuries ago to confuse raiding pirates.
attractions.tip: Getting lost in the old town's lanes is part of the experience — most paths eventually lead back to the waterfront.

attractions.name: The windmills (Kato Mili)

image.alt: The historic windmills overlooking Mykonos Town

attractions.text: A row of white stone windmills overlooking the town and Little Venice, once used to mill wheat and now the island's single most photographed landmark.
attractions.tip: The area around the windmills offers excellent sunset views over Little Venice below.

attractions.name: Little Venice

image.alt: Little Venice's waterfront houses with balconies over the sea

attractions.text: A row of colourful waterfront houses with balconies hanging directly over the sea, reminiscent of Venice's own canal-side architecture.
attractions.tip: Several of the waterfront buildings are now bars, offering a good excuse to enjoy the view with a drink.

attractions.name: Panagia Paraportiani

image.alt: The whitewashed Panagia Paraportiani church complex

attractions.text: A striking cluster of five whitewashed churches fused into one asymmetrical structure, among the most photographed churches in Greece.
attractions.tip: Early morning light gives the church's white curves a soft, dramatic quality for photographs.

attractions.name: Delos archaeological site

image.alt: Ancient ruins on the sacred island of Delos

attractions.text: A short boat trip reaches this uninhabited island, considered one of the ancient Greek world's most sacred sites and a significant UNESCO World Heritage Site.
attractions.tip: Bring water and sun protection — the island is exposed with very little shade across its ruins.

attractions.name: Ano Mera village

image.alt: The Panagia Tourliani Monastery in Ano Mera

attractions.text: A quieter inland village away from the coast, home to the historic Panagia Tourliani Monastery and a real sense of pre-tourism Mykonos life.
attractions.tip: The village's central square offers good, less touristy taverna options than the coast.

thingsToDoIntro: Beyond the old town, Mykonos rewards its beach club culture, its nightlife and the ancient island just offshore.

thingsToDo.title: Spend a day at Paradise or Super Paradise beach

image.alt: Paradise beach, one of Mykonos' famous beach club beaches

thingsToDo.text: The island's most famous beach clubs, central to Mykonos' party reputation, with music, sunbeds and beachside bars running throughout the day.
thingsToDo.tip: Book sunbeds ahead in peak season at the most popular clubs, which fill by mid-morning.

thingsToDo.title: Watch the sunset from Little Venice

image.alt: Little Venice's waterfront bars, a classic Mykonos sunset spot

thingsToDo.text: An essential Mykonos evening, watching the sun set over the water from one of the waterfront bars beneath the windmills.
thingsToDo.tip: Arrive with enough time to find a good seat — the best-positioned bars fill quickly as sunset approaches.

thingsToDo.title: Day trip to Delos

image.alt: Ruins spread across the island of Delos

thingsToDo.text: An essential piece of ancient history a short boat ride away, with ruins spanning temples, mosaics and an entire ancient sacred precinct.
thingsToDo.tip: Boats run a limited schedule — check return times carefully to avoid being stranded past the last crossing.

thingsToDo.title: Get lost in Mykonos Town's lanes

image.alt: A narrow whitewashed lane in Mykonos Town

thingsToDo.text: The old town's labyrinthine streets reward simply wandering without a fixed destination, discovering small shops and quiet corners.
thingsToDo.tip: The area known as 'Little Venice' and the streets just behind it hold some of the town's most photogenic corners.

thingsToDo.title: Experience Mykonos' nightlife
thingsToDo.text: From sunset cocktail bars to late-night clubs, Mykonos' nightlife scene is central to the island's international reputation.
thingsToDo.tip: Many of the island's famous clubs don't get busy until well after midnight — pace the evening accordingly.

thingsToDo.title: Try windsurfing or watersports

image.alt: A windsurfer on a Greek island beach

thingsToDo.text: Mykonos' reliable winds make it a well-regarded windsurfing and kitesurfing destination, with several beaches offering lessons and rentals.
thingsToDo.tip: Kalafatis beach on the island's eastern side is the most established watersports hub.

foodIntro: Mykonos' food culture centres on genuine Cycladic specialities alongside the island's own cured meats and cheese.

foods.name: Louza
foods.text: Cured, spiced pork loin, a genuine Mykonos specialty traditionally air-dried and thinly sliced, similar in spirit to Italian cured meats.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional tavernas and delicatessens throughout the island, often served as part of a meze spread.

foods.name: Kopanisti

image.alt: Kopanisti, a spicy whipped Cycladic cheese

foods.text: A spicy, tangy whipped cheese made from fermented local cheese, a genuine Mykonos and wider Cyclades specialty distinct from milder Greek cheeses.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional tavernas across the island, often served as a dip with bread.

foods.name: Mykonian sausage (loukaniko)
foods.text: A distinctive local sausage, seasoned with orange peel and local spices, grilled and served as a taverna staple.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional tavernas throughout Mykonos Town and Ano Mera.

foods.name: Fresh seafood

image.alt: Grilled octopus, a classic Greek island seafood dish

foods.text: Grilled octopus, fresh fish and shellfish, excellent around the island's harbourside restaurants, typically priced by weight.
foods.whereToTry: Harbourside tavernas in Mykonos Town and the smaller fishing village of Ornos.

foods.name: Amygdalota
foods.text: Soft almond-based sweets, popular across the Cyclades, often dusted with powdered sugar and shaped by hand.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional bakeries and sweet shops throughout Mykonos Town.

foods.name: Local Cycladic wine
foods.text: Mykonos' own small wine production, alongside wines from neighbouring islands, worth trying at a taverna's house selection.
foods.whereToTry: Tavernas across the island, many offering a good regional wine list.

accommodation.intro: Mykonos' accommodation spans the old town's central energy to quieter beachside resort areas.

areas.name: Mykonos Town
areas.bestFor: Walking to the sights and nightlife
areas.text: The most central, atmospheric base, putting Little Venice, the windmills and old town restaurants within easy walking distance.

areas.name: Platis Gialos or Ornos
areas.text: Established beach resort areas with good bus connections to Mykonos Town.

areas.name: Near Paradise or Super Paradise
areas.text: Puts the island's most famous party beaches directly on your doorstep, at a genuine premium for peak season.

gettingThere.intro: Mykonos is reached by short flight or ferry from Athens, both well served in season.

options.text: A short flight from [[athens|Athens]] reaches Mykonos in about 40 minutes, considerably faster than the ferry alternative.
options.detail: Book ahead in peak summer, when popular flight times can sell out or spike in price.

options.text: High-speed ferries from [[athens|Athens]]' port reach Mykonos in about 3 hours, with slower conventional ferries also available.
options.detail: Book high-speed ferries ahead in July and August, when popular Cyclades routes can sell out.

options.text: Direct ferries connect Mykonos to [[santorini|Santorini]] in about 2–3 hours and to [[crete|Crete]] with a longer connection.
options.detail: Routes and frequency vary by season — check current schedules before finalising an island-hopping itinerary.

gettingAround.intro: Mykonos Town is walkable, with buses and taxis covering the wider island's beaches.

options.text: A reasonably frequent network connects Mykonos Town to the island's main beaches, including Paradise and Platis Gialos.
options.detail: Buses can be crowded in peak season and at popular beach departure times.

options.text: Offers genuine flexibility for reaching quieter northern beaches and Ano Mera at your own pace.
options.detail: Mykonos Town's narrow lanes are largely pedestrian — park at the edge of town rather than attempting to drive in.

options.text: Seasonal boat services connect several of the island's southern beaches directly by sea.
options.detail: A scenic alternative to the bus, particularly between the beach-club beaches.

bestTime.headline: May–June and September, for warm weather without peak crowds
bestTime.summary: Mykonos' summer nightlife and beach club scene peak hard in July and August, and shoulder season offers a quieter, more affordable version of the island.

seasons.text: Mild, increasingly warm weather with beach clubs reopening and crowds well below the summer peak.
Hot, lively and at the height of its party reputation, but also the island's most crowded and expensive months.
Warm sea temperatures and a winding-down nightlife scene, with meaningfully thinner crowds than August.
Quiet, with most beach clubs, bars and many hotels closed for the season.

bestTime.avoid: Peak July and August without accommodation booked many months ahead — Mykonos' rooms fill early and prices spike considerably during its busiest party season.

itinerary.title: Three days in Mykonos
itinerary.intro: The old town and windmills first, then Delos, then the island's famous beaches.

days.title: Mykonos Town and Little Venice
days.morning: Wander the old town's lanes and Panagia Paraportiani.
days.evening: Sunset drinks in Little Venice, then dinner in town.

days.title: Delos day trip
days.summary: Ancient history a short boat ride away.
days.morning: Boat to Delos and explore the ancient ruins.

days.title: Beach day
days.morning: Travel to Paradise or Super Paradise beach.
days.evening: A final dinner in Ano Mera or back in town.

tipsIntro: Practical notes on timing, booking and etiquette that make a real difference to a Mykonos trip.
tips: Book accommodation many months ahead for July and August — Mykonos' rooms sell out and prices spike early.
Book beach club sunbeds ahead at the most popular spots, which fill by mid-morning in peak season.
Check Delos boat schedules carefully — services are limited and missing the last return crossing is a genuine inconvenience.
Wear comfortable shoes for Mykonos Town's marble-paved lanes, which can be slippery when wet.
Consider Platis Gialos or Ornos over the very centre of town for a quieter, better-value stay with easy bus access.
Bring cash for smaller tavernas and beach vendors, some of which remain cash-preferring even on this well-touristed island.
Pack for genuine wind — the strong meltemi winds common in summer can affect beach comfort and boat schedules alike.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Mykonos?
faq.a: Three works well — enough for the old town, a Delos day trip and at least one full beach day without feeling rushed.

faq.q: Is Mykonos only about nightlife and beach clubs?
faq.a: No — the old town's architecture, Delos' ancient history and the island's quieter northern beaches all stand on their own beyond the party reputation.
Yes, among Greece's most expensive islands, particularly for beach club sunbeds and accommodation in July and August.

faq.q: What is the best time of year to visit?
faq.a: May to June and September offer warm weather with meaningfully lower crowds and prices than July and August, which are the island's busiest, most expensive party months.

faq.q: Is Mykonos suitable for a quieter, non-party trip?
faq.a: Yes — basing away from the main party beaches, visiting in shoulder season, and focusing on the old town, Delos and quieter beaches all make for a considerably calmer visit.
